scope: Known startup failure must retain and observe the original owned child close despite an IPC/control error. No generic native/process hardening.

evidence.failure: Fixed product runtime reported unable to open database file. stop() then threw EPIPE before awaiting close; diagnostic captured childExited=false and rethrew without final owner observation.
evidence.historicalOriginalClosure: UNKNOWN: no later original-child close or cleanup proof exists in this index. New tests or different children cannot resolve it.
evidence.databaseCause: Long temporary path correlates with failures; short temporary path checks passed. Exact OS/path/database cause is not established and is outside this repair.

defects.detail: child.connected is a snapshot; child.send may throw or fail after that check. The request precedes the close wait and stopRequested assignment, so EPIPE bypasses original-close observation.
completion rejects on any child error, including an IPC/control error, before the original close event. Catching send alone therefore cannot fix the ownership obligation.

design: Keep startup-ready error handling separate from original-close observation. A lifetime child error listener records control/child error diagnostics but does not settle the original-close obligation. Only the original child close event supplies code/signal/cleanup facts; marker publication may still report its own error after close.

Mark a stop request before attempting IPC. Use a guarded send with an error callback and a synchronous catch; retain bounded diagnostics for either control failure. Regardless of send success, disconnection, or control error, await the same original completion with the existing 120-second deadline. No PID adoption, fallback kill, invented close, or new timeout policy.

Preserve token-checked marker publication and claim provenance. CLOSED requires cleanup=true, exit code 0 and null signal exactly as today. A real close with exit code 1 is an observed close but remains UNKNOWN/quarantined; it must not authorize relaunch or credential reseeding.

Retain the original startup error and owner on the aggregate failure. After observed non-successful close, owner.completion remains available with the original close facts even though start/stop correctly rejects. Expose no arbitrary child script/import option.

regressions.purpose: Deterministic control-error versus close ordering through the actual startProduct path.
regressions.fixture: Scoped node:child_process fork mock plus syncBuiltinESMExports, restored in finally and nonconcurrent; return a test-owned EventEmitter child with stdout/stderr streams. Production fork target/options remain fixed.
assertions: Emit a startup failed message, then force stop send to throw EPIPE or report callback/error-event EPIPE before a delayed close; cover both synchronous and asynchronous control failures as finite subcases.
Startup cleanup must remain pending until that exact child close; a child error alone cannot discharge completion.

After original close code 1, original owner completion reports code/signal/cleanup facts; startup still rejects, owner marker UNKNOWN and claim retained. No cleanup success inferred from control error.

regressions.purpose: Actual fixed-runtime startup failure and original-close binding without AI or historical child adoption.
regressions.fixture: Start a test-owned loopback listener on an ephemeral port and request veyviz-catalog on that already-bound port, using the ordinary reviewed built artifact and a short test-owned temporary data root. Close only this test listener in finally.
assertions: The fixed child fails startup after runtime creation and follows its cleanup path; startProduct rejects with its original owner.
Await that owner's original completion and inspect the token-bound persisted marker; nonzero close remains UNKNOWN with claim retained even if partial runtime cleanup was reported.
A subsequent launch cannot reseed or silently reuse that quarantined generation. No claim that this new child proves closure of the old database-failure diagnostic.

validationProposal: Capture these two owners and launcher identity before/after execution.
Build current admitted product source before focused lifecycle tests; preserve raw logs and all failed attempts.
Run the bounded lifecycle regression and existing lifecycle cases; coordinator records the eventual required full npm test and wider product qualification separately.
compatibility: Launcher changes are fingerprint inputs, so they create a new reviewed generation. Existing credential/enrollment and UNKNOWN-generation refusal rules remain intact.
reviewLimitations: Read-only source and recorded-evidence inspection. No commands/tests/browser/child manipulation executed by reviewer, no new acceptance or admission asserted. Root owns exact implementation admission and shared Brain.

admission.authority: User fix all; root delegates the two already-contracted product owners to product Brawn for the concrete observed cleanup defect.
rules: Preserve all other product and foreign intelligence edits. Do not edit maintained framework source, original Veyviz repositories or private profiles.
Use a new bounded two-file overlay of the already verified snapshot; do not mutate its preserved baseline. Fresh build and lifecycle tests use short test-owned temp roots.
No full suite/model/browser execution until root integration. Historical unknown original child closure cannot be resolved by new tests.
